Redundant instance refreshes (with IAM auth)
### Bug Description

Hi, after #890, number of refreshes dropped and it is much better. However, I noticed that a lot of refreshes still occur just before token expiration. It happens every 30 second (rate limiter in `Instance`) for those 4 minutes ([refresh-buffer](https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/cloud-sql-python-connector/blob/2a955322251a22e8c8b9d2494209b6db94b0d14d/google/cloud/sql/connector/refresh_utils.py#L36)) just before IAM token expiration.

The problem is that [here](https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/cloud-sql-python-connector/blob/2a955322251a22e8c8b9d2494209b6db94b0d14d/google/cloud/sql/connector/instance.py#L337), expiration is set to lower value of ephemeral cert or IAM credentials. But IAM credentials are refreshed only when they are invalid [here](https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/cloud-sql-python-connector/blob/2a955322251a22e8c8b9d2494209b6db94b0d14d/google/cloud/sql/connector/refresh_utils.py#L91) (or in get-ephemeral, but metadata are refreshed first).

Ephemeral cert expiration is usually 1 hour so let's say that we request instance refresh 30 minutes before IAM token expiration.
Expiration value sent to `_seconds_until_refresh()` computation will always be set to IAM token expiration because now it is just 30  minutes (and fewer) and its lower than ephemeral cert 1h. When it's less than 4 minutes before expiration, [this condition](https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/cloud-sql-python-connector/blob/main/google/cloud/sql/connector/refresh_utils.py#L228) applies and seconds-until refresh starts returning `0` - meaning, refresh is performed instantly (well, with 30 seconds rate limiter). And this repeats every 30 seconds until IAM token is refreshed.

I don't know why expiration is set to IAM token expiration, can't we remove [this block](https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/cloud-sql-python-connector/blob/2a955322251a22e8c8b9d2494209b6db94b0d14d/google/cloud/sql/connector/instance.py#L333-L337)? Ephemeral cert should be valid even when IAM token expired, shouldn't it?

I checked the golang implementation and it refreshes IAM token [always](https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/cloud-sql-go-connector/blob/8a1e5218b018ee1ef1134a6b3ee3f5671a106885/internal/cloudsql/refresh.go#L164), not only when it is invalid.

The point is, 4 minutes before IAM token expiration, next refresh is computed based on IAM token, but IAM token is not actually refreshed, only ephemeral cert is refreshed but it's expiration time is not considered when scheduling next refresh, so it keeps refreshing ephemeral cert but schedules next refresh based on IAM token again and again until IAM expires.

I would create a PR but I was not sure if my first suggestion (don't set expiration to IAM token) is OK, it worked just fine in my project, but maybe I missed something about tokens and their validity. I would probably go with the second suggestion (always refresh IAM) as it is already used in go and also [cloud-sql-proxy](https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/cloud-sql-proxy) which I used as well and saw no problem with it (but Go refreshes token only in get-ephemeral, not in get-metadata).

(For sake of completeness of my ideas, the third option is to refresh IAM token in [_get_metadata](https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/cloud-sql-python-connector/blob/main/google/cloud/sql/connector/refresh_utils.py#L91) (and `_get_ephemeral`) when it is just about to expire, i.e. `credentials.expiry - utcnow() < _refresh_buffer`, if you don't want to refresh it always, but note that "always" means just once an hour (considering default expiration is 1h) so I think "refresh always" is simpler in this case and number of refreshes is same).


### Steps to reproduce?

You can use my code from #890. You have to find out when your IAM token expires and then run the script at least for that long. Refresh logs should appear every 30 seconds for 4 minutes before IAM token expiration.

```py
import logging
import time

import google.cloud.sql.connector
import sqlalchemy

instance_logger = logging.getLogger(name='google.cloud.sql.connector.instance')
instance_logger.setLevel(logging.DEBUG)

logging.basicConfig(format='%(asctime)s [%(levelname)s]: %(message)s')
logging.debug('test start')

connector = google.cloud.sql.connector.Connector()
def getconn():
    return connector.connect(
        "<project>:<region>:<db-name>",
        "pg8000",
        user="<username>",
        db="<db-name>",
        enable_iam_auth=True,
        ip_type=google.cloud.sql.connector.IPTypes.PRIVATE,
    )

pool = sqlalchemy.create_engine("postgresql+pg8000://", creator=getconn)

while True:
    with pool.connect() as db_conn:
        db_conn.execute(sqlalchemy.text("SELECT 1"))
    time.sleep(5)
```

### Environment

1. OS type and version: Linux, but this should not matter :)
2. Python version: 3.10
3. Cloud SQL Python Connector version:  current `main`, with #890 merged.

+def poly_loss_cross_entropy(
+    logits: chex.Array,
+    labels: chex.Array,
+    epsilon: float = 2.0,
+) -> chex.Array:
+  """Computes the PolyLoss between logits and labels.
+
+  PolyLoss is a variant of cross-entropy that adds an adjustable linear term
+  in (1-P_t), where P_t is the predicted probability of the true class.
+  Setting epsilon=0 yields identical results to softmax_cross_entropy.
+
+  References:
+    [PolyLoss](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2204.12511.pdf)
+
+  Args:
+    logits: Unnormalized log probabilities, with shape `[..., num_classes]`.
+    labels: Valid probability distributions (non-negative, sum to 1), e.g. a
+      one hot encoding specifying the correct class for each input;
+      must have a shape broadcastable to `[..., num_classes]`.
+    epsilon: Coefficient for the first polynomial term. Can be positive, zero,
+      or negative. When 0, the function reduces to standard softmax
+      cross-entropy. Default is 2.0.
+
+  Returns:
+    PolyLoss between each prediction and the corresponding target
+    distributions, with shape `[...]`. Equal to
+    `softmax_cross_entropy(logits, labels) + epsilon * (1 - P_t)` where
+    `P_t` is the predicted probability of the true class.
+  """
+  chex.assert_type([logits], float)
+  # Compute standard softmax cross entropy
+  cross_entropy = -jnp.sum(labels * jax.nn.log_softmax(logits, axis=-1), axis=-1)
+  # Compute P_t: probability of the true class
+  probs = jax.nn.softmax(logits, axis=-1)
+  P_t = jnp.sum(labels * probs, axis=-1)
+  # Return PolyLoss
+  return cross_entropy + epsilon * (1 - P_t)

issue_context:
Support non-standard "use exports field for directory resolution" behavior
Vite currently uses `exports` field when resolving directory specifiers.
For example, when `import './dir'` is written, Vite uses `exports` field of `./dir/package.json` if exists.

Node.js does not use `exports` field in this case (https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/58827). While Vite probably should not have supported this, there are some code that relies on this behavior ([nuxt](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/blob/a7d21ece19e69703aac5fbb1f7bf53f0dfc5751f/test/setup-env.ts#L3), [Vitest](https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/blob/176133ed0cc5c8d04d0faa2e58d4a4f9cf3b78a6/test/core/test/resolve-web.test.ts#L4-L5)). We prefer to not break these if possible.

To achieve that, it would be nice if oxc-resolver adds an option that opt-in to this behavior.

```
1,,2,
1,,2,
```

Python Jinja2 output

1,,2,

```

- Versions of minijinja: 2.9.0, 2.10.2

## What did you expect

I expected MiniJinja and Python Jinja2 to behave the same for this case.

## Description of the problem
Most of our utils modules are not really intended to be used by end-users , but should be used via high-level interfaces that call these methods.

+"""Provides basic checks to be reused in other modules."""
+from __future__ import annotations

+from collections.abc import Sized
+from typing import Any

+import numpy as np

+
+def check_no_zeros(variable: Any, name: str = 'variable') -> None:
+    """Check if variable, or if it is iterable, any of its components are zero.
+
+    Parameters
+    ----------
+    variable: Any
+        Variable to check for zeros.
+
+    name: str
+        Name of variable to be used in error message. (default: 'variable')
+    """
+    # construct error message first
+    error_message = f'{name} must not be zero'
+
+    # ducktyping check if variable is iterable
+    try:
+        _ = iter(variable)
+
+    # variable is not iterable, simple check for zero
+    except TypeError as exception:
+        if variable == 0:
+            raise ValueError(error_message) from exception
+
+    # variable is iterable, check each element for zero
+    else:
+        error_message = 'each component in ' + error_message
+
+        for variable_component in variable:
+            if variable_component == 0:
+                raise ValueError(error_message)
+
+
+def check_nan_both_channels(arr: np.ndarray) -> None:

+    """
+    # sanity check: horizontal and vertical gaze coordinates missing
+    # values at the same time (Eyelink eyetracker never records only
+    # one coordinate)
+    if not np.array_equal(np.isnan(arr[:, 0]), np.isnan(arr[:, 1])):
+        raise ValueError(

+        )

+def check_shapes(**kwargs: Any) -> None:

+
+    Raises
+    ------
+    ValueError
+        If any of the arrays is not of shape ``(N, 2)`` or if the shapes are not equal.
+    """
+    for key, array in kwargs.items():
+        if array.ndim != 2 or array.shape[1] != 2:
+            raise ValueError(f'{key} must have shape (N, 2) but have shape {array.shape}')

+    # Check if shapes are equal, printing the key of the first array that is not equal

+"""Provides path specific funtions."""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import re
+from pathlib import Path
+
+
+def get_filepaths(
+        path: str | Path,
+        extension: str | list[str] | None = None,
+        regex: re.Pattern | None = None,
+) -> list[Path]:
+    """Get filepaths from rootpath depending on extension or regular expression.
+
+    Passing extension and regex is mutually exclusive.
+
+    Parameters
+    ----------
+    path: str | Path
+        Root path to be traversed.
+    extension: str | list[str] | None
+        File extension to be filtered for. (default: None)
+    regex: re.Pattern | None
+        Regular expression filenames will be filtered for. (default: None)
+
+    Returns
+    -------
+    list[Path]
+
+    Raises
+    ------
+    ValueError
+        If both extension and regex is being passed.
+    """
+    if extension is not None and regex is not None:
+        raise ValueError('extension and regex are mutually exclusive')
+
+    if extension is not None and isinstance(extension, str):
+        extension = [extension]
+
+    path = Path(path)
+    if not path.is_dir():
+        return []
+
+    filepaths = []
+    for childpath in path.iterdir():
+        if childpath.is_dir():
+            filepaths.extend(get_filepaths(path=childpath, extension=extension, regex=regex))
+        else:
+            # if extension specified and not matching, continue to next
+            if extension and childpath.suffix not in extension:
+                continue
+            # if regex specified and not matching, continue to next
+            if regex and not regex.match(childpath.name):
+                continue
+            filepaths.append(childpath)
+    return filepaths
+
+
+def match_filepaths(
+        path: str | Path,
+        regex: re.Pattern,
+        relative: bool = True,
+        relative_anchor: Path | None = None,
+) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
+    """Traverse path and match regular expression.
+
+    Parameters
+    ----------
+    path: str | Path
+        Root path to be traversed.
+    regex: re.Pattern
+        Regular expression filenames will be matched against.
+    relative: bool
+        If True, specify filepath as relative to root path. (default: True)
+    relative_anchor: Path | None
+        Specifies root path in case of ``relative == True``. If None, ``path`` will be chosen
+        as `relative_anchor` for recursive calls. (default: None)
+
+    Returns
+    -------
+    list[dict[str, str]]
+        Each entry contains the match group dictionary of the regular expression.
+
+    Raises
+    ------
+    ValueError
+        If ``path`` does not point to a directory.
+    """
+    path = Path(path)
+
+    if not path.exists():
+        raise ValueError(f'path does not exist (path = {path})')
+
+    if not path.is_dir():
+        raise ValueError(f'path must point to a directory (path = {path})')
+
+    if relative and relative_anchor is None:
+        relative_anchor = path
+
+    match_dicts: list[dict[str, str]] = []
+    for childpath in path.iterdir():
+        if childpath.is_dir():
+            recursive_results = match_filepaths(
+                path=childpath, regex=regex,
+                relative=relative, relative_anchor=relative_anchor,
+            )
+            match_dicts.extend(recursive_results)
+        elif match := regex.match(childpath.name):
+            match_dict = match.groupdict()
+
+            filepath = childpath
+            if relative:
+                # mypy is unaware that 'relative_anchor' can never be None (l.116)
+                assert relative_anchor is not None
+                filepath = filepath.relative_to(relative_anchor)
+
+            match_dict['filepath'] = str(filepath)
+            match_dicts.append(match_dict)
+    return match_dicts

+"""Provides string specific funtions."""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import re
+
+CURLY_TO_REGEX = re.compile(
+    r'(?:^|(?<=[^{])|(?<={{)){(?P<name>[^{][0-9a-zA-z_]*?)(?:\:(?P<quantity>\d*)(?P<type>[sd])?)?}',
+)
+
+
+def curly_to_regex(s: str) -> re.Pattern:
+    """Return regex pattern converted from provided python formatting style pattern.
+
+    By default all parameters are strings, if you want to specify number you can do: {num:d}
+    If you want to specify parameter's length you can do: {two_symbols:2} or {four_digits:4d}
+    Characters { and } can be escaped the same way as in python: {{ and }}
+    For example:
+                r'{subject_id:d}_{session_name}.csv'
+    converts to r'(?P<subject_id>[0-9]+)_(?P<session_name>.+).csv'
+
+    Parameters
+    ----------
+    s: str
+        Pattern in python formatting style.
+
+    Returns
+    -------
+    re.Pattern
+        Converted regex patterns.
+    """
+
+    def replace_aux(match: re.Match) -> str:     # Auxiliary replacement function
+        pattern = r'.'
+        if match.group('type') == 'd':
+            pattern = r'[0-9]'
+        elif match.group('type') == 's':
+            pattern = r'.'
+        quantity = r'+'
+        if match.group('quantity'):
+            quantity = f'{{{match.group("quantity")}}}'
+        return fr'(?P<{match.group("name")}>{pattern}{quantity})'
+
+    result = CURLY_TO_REGEX.sub(replace_aux, s)
+    result = result.replace('{{', '{').replace('}}', '}')
+    return re.compile(result)

issue_context:
Enhance multi-command documentation
When array-syntax support was added for specifying multiple commands the documentation was updated to describe the new behavior. However, this could potentially be misleading and give the impression that's the _only_ way to run multiple commands (as opposed to using `&&`.

We should enhance the docs to be more explicit about specifying the different options, and clarify that the array syntax is only supported in v0.12+

 ### Hooks
-Under the `[hooks]` table, you can add an entry for any and every git hook you want to run by adding a key using the name of the [git hook][git hooks], and then specify the command/script you want to run for that hook. Multiple commands in a form of a toml array are also allowed. Whenever that git hook is triggered, `rusty-hook` will run your specified command!
+Under the `[hooks]` table, you can add an entry for any and every git hook you want to run by adding a key using the name of the [git hook][git hooks], and then specify the command/script you want to run for that hook. There are two ways to specify multiple commands:
+
+1. **Using shell's `&&` operator** (supported in all versions):
+   ```toml
+   [hooks]
+   pre-push = "cargo check && cargo fmt -- --check"
+   ```
+
+2. **Using TOML array syntax** (supported in v0.12+):
+   ```toml
+   [hooks]
+   pre-push = ["cargo check", "cargo fmt -- --check"]
+   ```
+
+Whenever that git hook is triggered, `rusty-hook` will run your specified command!
 
 #### Using git arguments
 In git hook commands, any instance of `%rh!` will be replaced by the arguments that git passes to this hook.

issue_context:
Have an easy way to see if an entire ActionLike is disabled
## What problem does this solve?

https://github.com/Leafwing-Studios/leafwing-input-manager/pull/456 changed the way that disabling actions was handled, from using a `ToggleActions<A>` resource to adding a `disabled` flag **per Action** (not ActionState)
I think there still should be a way to disable an entire `ActionLike`.

Currently we only have the method `disabled(a: &Action)` to check if a given Action is disabled, but very often we would want to check quickly if the entire set of Actions is disabled for a given entity.

One use-case: in networking, if the entire set of actions is disabled, I would like to stop sending network packets for a given entity.
I guess currently I could iterate through all Actions and check if all of them are disabled, but that doesn't seem elegant.

## What solution would you like?

Maybe the `ActionState` should contain additional data that is shared between all Actions, on top of the existing HashMap
```
pub struct ActionState<A: Actionlike> {
    /// The [`ActionData`] of each action
    action_data: HashMap<A, ActionData>,
}
```

Something like
```
pub struct ActionState<A: Actionlike> {
    /// The [`ActionData`] of each action
    action_data: HashMap<A, ActionData>,
    disabled: bool,
}
```
(disabled could be a nested Metadata field)

Then I could easily disable the entire ActionState, instead of disabling each Action individually.



## Related work

Related to https://github.com/Leafwing-Studios/leafwing-input-manager/issues/553

[bug] Feedback for experimental Premake Generator (wxsqlite3)
### Describe the bug

Thank you for introducing the new Premake generator in [this pull request](https://github.com/conan-io/conan/pull/17898). I tested it by creating a recipe for [wxsqlite3](https://github.com/utelle/wxsqlite3) and encountered a few issues along the way. If it's not ready for testing yet, please let me know.

Prerequisites:

OS: Windows

I wanted to bring to your attention that I encountered two issues while running conan create on my wxsqlite3 recipe. I've addressed them with the patch file provided below.

The first issue is that Conan generates paths with backslashes, which are interpreted as escape characters—this seems to be a bug. watchmedo auto-restart behavior change with 2.1.9
We were using `watchmedo auto-restart` to call mypy and some flake8 tooling upon file changes. With the changes introduced by https://github.com/gorakhargosh/watchdog/pull/896, these processes re-run continually every time they exit whereas before they were re-ran upon a watched file/directory change.

The name `auto-restart` makes me believe that this is actually desirable behavior and perhaps we were misusing that sub-command, however there doesn't appear to be an alternative to get the behavior we once had. `watchmedo shell-command` only runs the command on change with no option to run it once _and also_ upon watched file change.

Is there a way to add a flag to `auto-restart` which only restarts on an exit code, or maybe a way to use `shell-command` to call the command initially and then repeat on a file change?

issue_context:
Stop storing supertraits in the `ItemTree`
Currently when we lower traits, we lower any supertrait bounds to where-clauses in the traits's `GenericParams`, but we *also* store them redundantly in the `bounds` field:

https://github.com/rust-analyzer/rust-analyzer/blob/f3aaae65553550cc9b7101a844ecbc3d426a1bef/crates/hir_def/src/item_tree.rs#L647

The field is only used to display the trait, so it should be removed. When displaying the trait, we currently display *both* the supertrait bounds, *and* all where-clauses in the `GenericParams`, so the supertrait bounds actually appear twice:

```rust
pub trait HirDisplay: Clone {}
```
results in:
```
pub trait HirDisplay: Clone
where
    Self: Clone,
```

issue_context:
Implement MSC1767 (Extensible events)
[Original MSC](https://github.com/matrix-org/matrix-doc/blob/matthew/msc1767/proposals/1767-extensible-events.md)

**Related MSCs**:
* [MSC3488 - Location data](https://github.com/matrix-org/matrix-doc/pull/3488)
* [MSC3381 - Polls](https://github.com/matrix-org/matrix-doc/pull/3381)
* [MSC3245 - Voice messages](https://github.com/matrix-org/matrix-doc/pull/3245)
* [MSC3246 - Audio (non-voice)](https://github.com/matrix-org/matrix-doc/pull/3246)
* [MSC3551 - Files](https://github.com/matrix-org/matrix-doc/pull/3551)
* [MSC3552 - Images and Stickers](https://github.com/matrix-org/matrix-doc/pull/3552)
* [MSC3553 - Videos](https://github.com/matrix-org/matrix-doc/pull/3553)
* [MSC3554 - Translatable text](https://github.com/matrix-org/matrix-doc/pull/3554)

MSC1767 seems to be pretty stable now, for the others it varies.

It's gonna change the way the JSON data is (de)serialized of course, but that could also make the types more reusable if we mirror this data structure. For example an `ImageMessageEventContent` could look like that:

```rust
pub struct ImageMessageEventContent {
    pub message: Option<Box<Message, Global>>,
    pub file: Option<Box<FileInfo, Global>>,
    pub image: Option<Box<ImageInfo, Global>>,
    pub thumbnail: Option<Box<ThumbnailInfo, Global>>,
    pub caption: Option<Box<Caption, Global>>,
}
```

In that case `FileInfo` is exactly the same for `m.image`, `m.file`, `m.audio`, `m.video`, etc. That means it's easier to use the same behaviours between message types without implementinf traits. This new data structure could be implemented at any time but it would break the current API.

Per the MSC, there are 3 (de)serialization scenarios to handle:
- Current "non-extensible" events. *These are the ones that should be sent when possible.*
- Transition events that keep the `m.room.message` type and add extensible events to the content. *These are the ones that could be received, and they are backwards-compatible.*
- Real extensible events that use only the new types. *These shouldn't appear until the end of the transition.*

issue_context:
Stripping `extern "Rust"` from functions
Rustfmt currently strips `extern "Rust"` from function signatures. e.g formatting `extern "Rust" fn foo() {}` to `fn foo() {}`. This seems to be intentional from the current code.

The problem here is this essentially deletes documentation from the code. Given a function such as:
```rust
#[no_mangle]
extern "Rust" fn foo() { /* do stuff */ }
```
With the ABI explicitly added here, it's clear that the odd ABI choice is intentional. Without the explicit ABI, it's unclear whether the choice was intentional, or an ABI was forgotten (e.g. `extern "C"`).

Can't find anything relevant from the style guide about this removal.

issue_context:
Consider streamlining the ActiveSpan::start API
We need to specify ambient properties upfront, but could give you a default completion and span properties, letting you override them through methods on the resulting `ActiveSpan`. This would cut the noise down for cases where you want a span, but don’t need to configure everything.

+/**
+Start a span.
+
+# Syntax
+
+```text
+(control_param),* tpl, (property),*
+```
+
+where
+
+- `control_param`: A Rust field-value with a pre-determined identifier (see below).
+- `tpl`: A template string literal.
+- `property`: A Rust field-value for a property to capture.
+
+# Control parameters
+
+This macro accepts the following optional control parameters:
+
+| name        | type                          | description                                                                                                                                                    |
+| ----------- | ----------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
+| `rt`        | `impl emit::runtime::Runtime` | The runtime to emit the event through.                                                                                                                         |
+| `mdl`       | `impl Into<emit::Path>`       | The module the event belongs to. If unspecified the current module path is used.                                                                               |
+| `when`      | `impl emit::Filter`           | A filter to use instead of the one configured on the runtime.                                                                                                  |
+| `panic_lvl` | `str` or `emit::Level`        | Detect whether the function panics and use the given level if it does.                                                                                         |
+
+# Template
+
+The template for the event. See the [`macro@tpl`] macro for syntax.
+
+# Properties
+
+Properties that appear within the template or after it are added to the emitted event. The identifier of the property is its key. Property capturing can be adjusted through the `as_*` attribute macros.
+
+# Returns
+
+A tuple `(guard, frame)` where:
+- `guard` is an `ActiveSpan` that can be used to complete the span.
+- `frame` is a `Frame` used to activate the span's ambient context.
+*/
+#[proc_macro]
+pub fn start_span(item: proc_macro::TokenStream) -> proc_macro::TokenStream {
+    span::expand_start_tokens(span::ExpandStartTokens {
+        level: None,
+        input: item.into(),
+    })
+    .unwrap_or_compile_error()
+}
+
+/**

+pub fn start_debug_span(item: proc_macro::TokenStream) -> proc_macro::TokenStream {

+    .unwrap_or_compile_error()

+        });
+        let mut mdl = Arg::new("mdl", |fv| {
+            let expr = &fv.expr;

+            Ok(args::MdlArg::new(quote_spanned!(expr.span()=> #expr)))
+        });
+        let mut when = Arg::new("when", |fv| {
+            let expr = &fv.expr;
+
+            Ok(args::WhenArg::new(quote_spanned!(expr.span()=> #expr)))
+        });
+        let mut panic_lvl = Arg::token_stream("panic_lvl", |fv| {
+            let expr = &fv.expr;
+
+            Ok(quote_spanned!(expr.span()=> #expr))
+        });

+        args::set_from_field_values(
+            input.parse_terminated(FieldValue::parse, Token![,])?.iter(),

+                &mut rt,
+                &mut when,
+                &mut panic_lvl,

+            rt: rt.take_or_default(),
+            mdl: mdl.take_or_default(),
+            when: when.take_or_default(),

+pub fn expand_start_tokens(opts: ExpandStartTokens) -> Result<TokenStream, syn::Error> {
+    let span = opts.input.span();
+
+    let (args, template, ctxt_props) =
+        template::parse2::<StartArgs>(opts.input, capture::default_fn_name, false)?;
+
+    check_evt_props(&ctxt_props)?;
+
+    let template =
+        template.ok_or_else(|| syn::Error::new(span, "missing template string literal"))?;
+
+    let rt_tokens = args.rt.to_tokens()?.to_ref_tokens();
+    let mdl_tokens = args.mdl.to_tokens();
+    let when_tokens = args
+        .when
+        .to_tokens()
+        .map(|when| when.to_ref_tokens())
+        .to_option_tokens(quote!(&emit::Empty));
+
+    let ctxt_props_tokens = ctxt_props.props_tokens().to_ref_tokens();
+    let template_tokens = template.template_tokens().to_ref_tokens();
+    let span_name_tokens = template.template_literal_tokens();
+
+    let default_lvl_tokens = opts.level;
+    let panic_lvl_tokens = args.panic_lvl;
+
+    // Build the completion function
+    // The level is passed as Option<&Level>
+    let lvl_tokens = default_lvl_tokens
+        .as_ref()
+        .map(|lvl| lvl.to_ref_tokens())
+        .to_option_tokens(quote!(&emit::Level));
+
+    let panic_lvl_tokens = panic_lvl_tokens
+        .map(|lvl| lvl.to_ref_tokens())
+        .to_option_tokens(quote!(&emit::Level));
+
+    let default_completion_tokens = quote!(emit::span::completion::from_fn(|span| {
+        emit::__private::__private_complete_span(
+            #rt_tokens,
+            span,
+            #template_tokens,
+            #lvl_tokens,
+            #panic_lvl_tokens,
+        )
+    }));
+
+    // For __private_begin_span, the level needs to be passed as a reference
+    // So if there's a level, we pass Some(&Level::Debug) etc.
+    let lvl_arg = default_lvl_tokens
+        .map(|lvl| quote!(&#lvl))
+        .to_option_tokens(quote!(&emit::Level));
+
+    Ok(quote!({
+        emit::__private::__private_begin_span(
+            #rt_tokens,
+            #mdl_tokens,
+            #span_name_tokens,
+            #lvl_arg,
+            #when_tokens,
+            #ctxt_props_tokens,
+            #default_completion_tokens,
+        )
+    }))
+}

issue_context:
migrate `set` to `query_mut`
Today, to set the value of a query, you do `db.query(Q).set(...)`. 

To build on https://github.com/salsa-rs/salsa/pull/78, we would like to change this to `db.query_mut(Q).set(...)`. This would then require an `&mut self` on the database.

Together with https://github.com/salsa-rs/salsa/pull/78, this moves us completely to the model of "one mutator thread" (which owns the main database handle, of type `DB`) and various "reader threads" (which own `Frozen<DB>` handles). Only the mutator thread can get `&mut self` access to the DB, so only it can invoke `set`. 

I'll follow up with mentoring instructions perhaps.

+import base64
+
+
+def safe_b64encode(s):
+    """
+    Returns a base64 string for the supplied input, handling both
+    Unicode and byte inputs gracefully.
+
+    **Parameters**
+
+        ``s`` (*str* or *bytes*)
+          The text to be base64-encoded. If a `str`, it is encoded to UTF-8;
+          if a `bytes` object, it is used directly. UnicodeDecodeError from
+          UTF-8 encoding is caught and the original bytes are encoded instead.
+
+    **Returns**
+
+        ``str``
+          A UTF-8 decoded base64 representation of the input. Never raises
+          for Unicode issues; always returns a string.
+    """
+    if isinstance(s, str):
+        try:
+            # Try to encode the string as UTF-8
+            b = s.encode('utf-8')
+        except UnicodeDecodeError:
+            # If that fails (shouldn't happen for str), encode as latin-1
+            # which can encode any unicode code point
+            b = s.encode('latin-1')
+    else:
+        # It's already bytes, use directly
+        b = s
+    
+    # Encode using base64 and decode to get a string
+    return base64.b64encode(b).decode('utf-8')

issue_context:
RegexSet and Regex give different results for the same pattern in 1.9
#### What version of regex are you using?

`1.9.3`. The issue is present in regex `1.9.0` and later.

#### Describe the bug at a high level.

`RegexSet::new([r"(?m)^ *v [0-9]"]).unwrap().is_match("v 0")` incorrectly returns false in version 1.9.0 and later.

It returns true in 1.8.4.

It returns true if I use a `Regex` instead of a `RegexSet`.

#### What are the steps to reproduce the behavior?

```rust
fn main() {
    let pattern = r"(?m)^ *v [0-9]";
    let text = "v 0";

    let re = regex::Regex::new(pattern).unwrap();
    println!("re is: {re:?}");
    println!("{}", re.is_match(text)); // true (correct)

    let rs = regex::RegexSet::new([pattern]).unwrap();
    println!("rs is: {rs:?}");
    println!("{}", rs.is_match(text)); // false (incorrect)
}
```

([playground link](https://play.rust-lang.org/?version=stable&mode=debug&edition=2021&gist=eb964fd144925df0b5fd15e0d1d61279))

#### What is the actual behavior?

```
re is: Regex("(?m)^ *v [0-9]")
true
rs is: RegexSet(["(?m)^ *v [0-9]"])
false
```

#### What is the expected behavior?

The last line should be `true`.

### What
Change `Host` `check_same_env -> Result` to `Host` `is_same_env -> bool`.

### Why
The check function is used only in the SDK, not in the Env. In the SDK it is used in two ways:
1. To hard stop in tests when a value is used with the wrong Host where that use is unsupported.
2. To change the behaviour used when comparing vals across Envs which is the only cross-Env supported action.

In both cases the SDK is using the `Host` `check_same_env` to find out if the env is the same, and then the SDK is choosing to present that information in different ways either by panicking or branching.

Given that the SDK owns the presentation, and the Env is just providing information, the Env should provide this information plainly as a bool. The SDK can present the error however it needs.

This oddity was pointed out here:

> It also doesn't really make sense for `check` to be used in `is` and not vice versa. It would probably make more sense to expose the `is` function from env if we think it's necessary.

_Originally posted by @dmkozh in https://github.com/stellar/rs-soroban-sdk/pull/1467#discussion_r2094183786_

issue_context:
Make `-u` idempotent (always search all files/dirs)
`fd -u` is an alias for `fd -I`and `fd -uu`is an alias for `fd -IH`. The former is unnecessary given that it's an alias to another one-letter flag (I imagine it's there for historical reasons?) and the latter is cumbersome if someone wanted to use the long form (`--unrestricted`). This setup also makes the behavior of the flag ambiguous if new default filters were added in the future. In that case, would I disable all filters with `-uu` or would I need to use `-uuu`?

Given the project's focus on ergonomics and usability, I'd suggest to make `-u` always search all files and to deprecate `-uu`. This would be the equivalent of `ls -a`, giving the user the guarantee that no filters will be applied by default. The main cons of this suggestion is that it's a breaking change and a subtle one: the command would continue to work with `-u` but could return a different set of results.

issue_context:
RFE: Give Commit objects a replace method that returns new Commit with modified attributes
The `datetime` objects produced by Python's `datetime` module are immutable, much like `Commit` objects. The `datetime` module provides a convenient `replace` function that returns a new object based on an old with one or more attributes replaced.  E.g, I can write:

```
>>> d = datetime.datetime.now()
>>> d.replace(hour=0, minute=0, second=0)
datetime.datetime(2021, 2, 15, 0, 0, 0, 318021)
```

I would like to see the same api on `Commit` objects, so that one could write:

```
>>> newcommit = oldcommit.replace(message='This is a test', author='Cookie Monster')
```
patch:
diff --git a/git/objects/commit.py b/git/objects/commit.py
index 302798c..ca5fbc0 100644
--- a/git/objects/commit.py
+++ b/git/objects/commit.py
@@ -132,6 +132,62 @@ class Commit(base.Object, Iterable, Diffable, Traversable, Serializable):
         if gpgsig is not None:
             self.gpgsig = gpgsig
 
+    def replace(self, **kwargs):
+        """Return a new commit object with some replaced attributes.
+
+        :param kwargs: keyword arguments whose names are members of Commit.__slots__
+            (e.g., message, author, author_email, committer, ...). Attributes not
+            supplied are copied from the original commit. Supplying a name not in
+            __slots__ triggers a ValueError.
+        :return: a new Commit object belonging to the same repository, with the
+            provided attributes replaced and a newly calculated SHA (accessible via
+            ``hexsha``).
+        :raises ValueError: for invalid attribute names.
+
+        This is analogous to ``datetime.replace``; useful for creating a modified
+        commit without mutating the original.
+        """
+        for key in kwargs:
+            if key not in self.__slots__:
+                raise ValueError("Invalid attribute name: %s" % key)
+
+        # Get all current attributes from the commit
+        # This will trigger loading of lazy attributes if needed
+        attrs = {}
+        for key in self.__slots__:
+            attrs[key] = getattr(self, key)
+
+        # Override with provided kwargs
+        attrs.update(kwargs)
+
+        # Create new commit with the modified attributes
+        new_commit = type(self)(
+            self.repo,
+            self.NULL_BIN_SHA,
+            tree=attrs['tree'],
+            author=attrs['author'],
+            authored_date=attrs['authored_date'],
+            author_tz_offset=attrs['author_tz_offset'],
+            committer=attrs['committer'],
+            committed_date=attrs['committed_date'],
+            committer_tz_offset=attrs['committer_tz_offset'],
+            message=attrs['message'],
+            parents=attrs['parents'],
+            encoding=attrs['encoding'],
+            gpgsig=attrs['gpgsig']
+        )
+
+        # Serialize and store to get new SHA
+        stream = BytesIO()
+        new_commit._serialize(stream)
+        streamlen = stream.tell()
+        stream.seek(0)
+
+        istream = self.repo.odb.store(IStream(type(new_commit).type, streamlen, stream))
+        new_commit.binsha = istream.binsha
+
+        return new_commit
+
     @classmethod
     def _get_intermediate_items(cls, commit):
         return commit.parents

6. Edit `dummy`

```

Creating project called `dummy`...

This is a common state to be in during PR CI scenarios.

Treating a checked out template as a folder, as opposed to a repo, would help a lot (https://github.com/cargo-generate/cargo-generate/issues/387) but not sure we'll fall into this check https://github.com/cargo-generate/cargo-generate/commit/d2211d28e8ad4d51856323e9ba7e7879dabae163. Ideally, a --directory or --folder parameter would be added instead of this fall-through behavior.

issue_context:
Add support for --whole-archive
See `man ld` for a description of what `--whole-archive` needs to do.

`--whole-archive` is a modifier that is pushed / popped by `--push-state` / `--pop-state`, so the value of the flag should be added to the `Modifiers` struct (in `args.rs`).

The method where the `whole_archive` attribute should be used is `ParsedInputObject::is_optional`.

It'd be good to have a test that verifies that `--whole-archive` is behaving as expected. There are probably a few ways such a test could be written. The key observation is that whatever is defined in the archive needs to not be directly referenced from the main test object, otherwise the archived object would be included even without `--whole-archive`. One option is to have an archive that puts something into a custom section, then have the `_start_` function check the custom section for that value. You can look at the test `custom_section.c` for how this is done.

Potential bug in separate_stains_macenko_pca.py | Function: argpercentile
Hi!

First off, thanks to all developers and maintainers for this amazing package!

I am using HistomicsTK on Ubuntu 20.04.5 LTS.

During my work with it I noticed a potential bug in the file `separate_stains_macenko_pca.py' in the function argpercentile.

https://github.com/DigitalSlideArchive/HistomicsTK/blob/15262df548a2579846a0dcfd8b7f41e30ddff58e/histomicstk/preprocessing/color_deconvolution/separate_stains_macenko_pca.py#L121C1-L125C41

For instance, this function is used in line 98 with a value for p = 0.99:
https://github.com/DigitalSlideArchive/HistomicsTK/blob/4748f9d2e00216a59056c1a75c87f65dc6b271aa/histomicstk/preprocessing/color_deconvolution/separate_stains_macenko_pca.py#L98C4-L98C56

With p = 0.99, as soon as the size of the provided array is smaller than 51, the calculated index will be larger than the length of the array. This leads to an "out of bounds" error in the subsequent call of numpy.argpartition(arr, i)[i] on line 125.

arr.size = 50, p = 0.99
i = 50 -> Will cause an error

I guess the easiest fix would be something like this:
```
i = int(p * arr.size + 0.5)
if i >= arr.size:
    i -= 1
return numpy.argpartition(arr, i)[i]
```

Having said all of this, I honestly am not sure if this combination of a small input array and a high percentage value is not supposed to occur in a normal application flow. Therefore, I am uncertain if this would merely mask another underlying problem.

Thank you for your time!

CosmWasm 2 address systems flaws
When [upgrading a complex codebase from 1.5 to 2.0](https://github.com/noislabs/nois-contracts/pull/302) I spend roughly 1 hour to make it compile but many more hours to make all the tests pass. The biggest issue is the change in the address validation in MockApi which does not allow arbitrary strings anymore. While I still think the change is good in general and new codebases will have an easier life, there are flaws we should address.
 
- [x] `mock_info` takes a `&str` address. However, we need a `Addr` in the caller code and an `Addr` in `MessageInfo`. Due to the `&str` type it is unclear if the input is supposed to contain the full address (it does). Thies leads to a log of `mock_info(manager2.as_str(), &[])` which could just be `mock_info(&manager2, &[])` if the type was `&Addr`. (https://github.com/CosmWasm/cosmwasm/pull/2160)
- [ ] `addr_make` cannot be used in `DepsMut` due to the way the API field is typed. Use case: shared functions like `setup_channel(deps.as_mut());`
- [x] #2211
- [x] Don't validate validator address in Multitest's `.add_validator(api, storage, &block, valoper1)` and probably also message delegate implementation. Validator addresses have a different layout than the account addresses. (https://github.com/CosmWasm/cw-multi-test/issues/173)

## Expected Behavior
Actix and its dependencies should have no known vulnerabilities unpatched

## Current Behavior
Actix is affected by [CVE-2020-8927](https://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2020-8927), buffer overflow in the Brotli C library, through `brotli-sys` crate.

## Possible Solution
There is no updated release of `brotli-sys` that fixes the issue ([it has been reported upstream](https://github.com/bitemyapp/brotli2-rs/issues/45)). There are several abandoned PRs updating to newer Brotli, so it looks like a new release will not be cut anytime soon.

The [`brotli` crate](https://crates.io/crates/brotli) provides a pure Rust implementation of Brotli compression and decompression. issue_context:
Efficiently map array to a (possibly) different type
[`ArrayBase::mapv_into()`](https://docs.rs/ndarray/0.15.3/ndarray/struct.ArrayBase.html#method.mapv_into) consumes self and reuses its memory allocation to compute a new array with the same shape and type.  Avoiding unnecessary allocations is important when mapping very large arrays.

When writing generic methods, it is often necessary to assume that two arrays may be of different types even though we might expect them to be the same type most of the time.  For example, a method that is generic over complex numbers may be called with all real arguments, all complex arguments, or a mixture of real and complex arguments.  This precludes direct use of `mapv_into()` since we cannot assume the arguments are the same type.

Would it be worth adding something like this [`trans_mapv_into()`](https://gist.github.com/benkay86/b9f3eea271999eccf158bfbbcd30b70e), which maps an array with elements of one type to a (possibly) different type?  If the types are the same it delegates to `mapv_into()`, and if the types are different it falls back to using additional allocations.  Type comparison is performed at runtime pending [specialization](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/31844).

Feature: Allow broker creation in on_startup hook
For some reason, I need to delay the creation of an app's broker in an `on_startup` hook. This is mainly because my application has a pretty heavy warmup bootstrap that loads a lot of data into memory so I need to delay this bootstrap (which actually includes broker creation) after the parent process forked into worker subprocesses, otherwise the parent process has an unnecessary high memory footprint (that only worker processes need to have).

E.g.

```python
from faststream import FastStream
from faststream.kafka import KafkaBroker

app = FastStream()

@app.on_startup
def bootstrap():
    app.set_broker(KafkaBroker(["localhost:9092"]))
    # some warmup of the application pre-loading data into memory
    ...
```

For now, this isn't working because of this assert https://github.com/airtai/faststream/blob/9b7c33e8765485cf28f850cb485afcd838c12079/faststream/app.py#L40 which occurs at the very begining of the workers run, before `on_startup` hooks are executed.

The example above is overly simplified and one could argue that broker could have been created outside the `bootstrap()` function, but, as per example at https://faststream.airt.ai/latest/getting-started/lifespan/hooks/#lifespan, it could be legitimate to create it based on environment setting specifying not only the broker host but also the kind of broker to use (nats, kafka, ...).

I currently solve the problem by providing an *empty* `KafkaBroker` at app instanciation (`app = FastStream(broker=KafkaBroker())`) before overriding it using `app.set_broker()` in the `bootstrap()` function.

However, as per the base `Application` constructor at https://github.com/airtai/faststream/blob/9b7c33e8765485cf28f850cb485afcd838c12079/faststream/_internal/application.py#L48-L70 which allows application instanciation without a defined broker and this comment in `Application.set_broker()` https://github.com/airtai/faststream/blob/9b7c33e8765485cf28f850cb485afcd838c12079/faststream/_internal/application.py#L117-L120 which claims to be used for creation/init in `on_startup`, I would have expected my use case to be legitimate.

### Describe the problem you'd like to have solved

<!--
> A clear and concise description of what the problem is. Ex. I'm always frustrated when [...]
-->
We've refactored our implementation of auth0 python in order to leverage the new asyncio support.
During the development, we've found difficult to  provide an aiohttp HTTP client session to the auth0 SDK, making difficult to leverage a best practice like https://docs.aiohttp.org/en/stable/faq.html#how-do-i-manage-a-clientsession-within-a-web-server


### Describe the ideal solution
Provide a way to inject a custom aiohttp client session that can be reused in a web server.
<!--
> A clear and concise description of what you want to happen.
-->

## Alternatives and current work-arounds
```
for name in modules.keys():
            module = getattr(auth0_client, name)
            module._async_client.client.set_session(SingletonAuth0AiohttpClientSession.get_aiohttp_client_session())
```
where the `SingletonAuth0AiohttpClientSession` is a class that is managed by FastAPI application events that automatically closes the session on the application shutdown.

+class AsyncAuth0(object):
+    """Provides easy access to all endpoint classes with async support
+
+    This class allows providing a custom aiohttp session for reuse
+    in web server applications.
+
+    Args:
+        domain (str): Your Auth0 domain, e.g: 'username.auth0.com'
+
+        token (str): Management API v2 Token
+
+        rest_options (RestClientOptions): Pass an instance of
+            RestClientOptions to configure additional RestClient
+            options, such as rate-limit retries.
+            (defaults to None)
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self, domain, token, rest_options=None):
+        self._session = None
+
+        for name, cls in modules.items():
+            cls = asyncify(cls)
+            setattr(
+                self,
+                name,
+                cls(domain=domain, token=token, rest_options=rest_options),
+            )
+
+    def set_session(self, session):
+        """Set a shared aiohttp ClientSession for all services.
+
+        This allows reusing the session across multiple calls,
+        which is a best practice for web servers.
+
+        Args:
+            session (aiohttp.ClientSession): An existing aiohttp ClientSession
+        """
+        self._session = session
+        for name in modules.keys():
+            module = getattr(self, name)
+            module._async_client.client.set_session(session)
+
+    async def __aenter__(self):
+        """Automatically create and set session within context manager."""
+        self._session = aiohttp.ClientSession()
+        for name in modules.keys():
+            module = getattr(self, name)
+            module._async_client.client.set_session(self._session)
+        return self
+
+    async def __aexit__(self, exc_type, exc_val, exc_tb):
+        """Automatically close session within context manager."""
+        if self._session:
+            await self._session.close()
+        self._session = None

+from typing import Dict, Any, Optional, Mapping, Iterable, Union

+class _CaselessDict(dict):
+    """
+    A dictionary that performs case-insensitive key lookups and operations.
+    
+    All string keys are treated case-insensitively for containment checks, 
+    item access, assignment, deletion, get and pop operations while preserving
+    the original key casing.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):
+        super().__init__()
+        # Map lowercase keys to original keys
+        self._lower_to_original = {}
+        # Initialize with provided data
+        if args:
+            if isinstance(args[0], Mapping):
+                for k, v in args[0].items():
+                    self._set_item(k, v)
+            elif isinstance(args[0], Iterable):
+                for k, v in args[0]:
+                    self._set_item(k, v)
+        for k, v in kwargs.items():
+            self._set_item(k, v)
+
+    def _set_item(self, key: str, value: Any):
+        """Set an item with case-insensitive key handling."""
+        lower_key = key.lower()
+        # Store the first encountered casing for each unique lowercase key
+        if lower_key not in self._lower_to_original:
+            self._lower_to_original[lower_key] = key
+        original_key = self._lower_to_original[lower_key]
+        super().__setitem__(original_key, value)
+
+    def _get_original_key(self, key: str) -> Optional[str]:
+        """Get the original key for a given lowercase key."""
+        return self._lower_to_original.get(key.lower())
+
+    def __contains__(self, key: Union[str, object]) -> bool:
+        if isinstance(key, str):
+            lower_key = key.lower()
+            return lower_key in self._lower_to_original
+        return super().__contains__(key)
+
+    def __getitem__(self, key: Union[str, object]) -> Any:
+        if isinstance(key, str):
+            original_key = self._get_original_key(key)
+            if original_key is not None:
+                return super().__getitem__(original_key)
+            # Key not found in caseless mapping
+            raise KeyError(key)
+        # For non-string keys, use standard dict behavior
+        return super().__getitem__(key)
+
+    def __setitem__(self, key: Union[str, object], value: Any):
+        if isinstance(key, str):
+            self._set_item(key, value)
+        else:
+            super().__setitem__(key, value)
+
+    def __delitem__(self, key: Union[str, object]):
+        if isinstance(key, str):
+            original_key = self._get_original_key(key)
+            if original_key is not None:
+                del self._lower_to_original[key.lower()]
+                super().__delitem__(original_key)
+                return
+            raise KeyError(key)
+        # For non-string keys, use standard dict behavior
+        super().__delitem__(key)
+
+    def get(self, key: Union[str, object], default: Any = None) -> Any:
+        if isinstance(key, str):
+            original_key = self._get_original_key(key)
+            if original_key is not None:
+                return super().__getitem__(original_key)
+        # For non-string keys, use standard dict behavior
+        return super().get(key, default)

+        if isinstance(key, str):
+            original_key = self._get_original_key(key)
+            if original_key is not None:
+                del self._lower_to_original[key.lower()]
+                return super().pop(original_key, *args)
+            if args:
+                return args[0]
+            raise KeyError(key)
+        # For non-string keys, use standard dict behavior
+        return super().pop(key, *args)
+

+        if isinstance(key, str):

+            if original_key is not None:

+            self._set_item(key, default)
+            return default
+        return super().setdefault(key, default)
+

+        if other is not None:

issue_context:
[CLI] `check-parse` command (or another command) should check parsing of entity data and schemas, not just policies
### Category

Other

### Describe the feature you'd like to request

Currently, the CLI `check-parse` command only checks the parsing of policies.

To check the parsing of entity data or schemas, you have to use other commands -- for instance `authorize` for entity data, or `validate` for schemas.  But this is inconvenient, as you also have to provide other inputs for those commands, like policies.  We don't have a dedicated way to check the parsing of entity data or schemas without also having to provide unnecessary inputs.

### Describe alternatives you've considered

We could have separate commands `check-policies-parse`, `check-entities-parse`, `check-schema-parse`; or (my preference) just have a single `check-parse` which checks that any or all of these parse.  `check-parse` could check the parsing of any or all of these in a single call -- e.g., if you pass just schema, it checks the parsing of the schema, or if you pass both entities and policies, it checks the parsing of the entities and policies; etc.

### Additional context

_No response_
